Even though the matter is listed for 'Hearing on Interlocutory Application' as both the learned counsel are ready to address their arguments as undertaken on the previous date of hearing, the matter is taken for final disposal.

2. Petitioner Nos.1 to 3, being accused Nos.2 to 4 have filed the petition under Articles 226 and 227 of the Constitution of India and also under Section 482 of Cr.PC, seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them in C.C.No.20004/2015, pending on the file of learned V Additional CMM, Bengaluru, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code ( in short IPC).

It is stated that during the pendency of the petition,
accused No.2 i.e., petitioner No.1 had died and the petition against him stands abated.

3. Brief facts of the case are that, respondent No.2 as informant filed the first information against accused Nos.1 to 4, alleging commission of the offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act.
It is stated that respondent No.2 married accused No.1 by registering their marriage in the Registrar office at NC: 2024:KHC:32199 Koramangala, Bengaluru on 28.11.2006.
Since her marriage, she was suffering from physical and mental abuse from accused Nos. 1 to 4, who were ill-treating her for not bringing sufficient dowry.
At the time of her marriage, she was working in IBM.
But after child birth, she was forced to resign from the job to take care of her child as there was no support from the family.

It is also stated that even during her pregnancy, she was tortured by her in-laws to sign the divorce papers for the reason that she belong to poor background and the in-laws i.e., accused Nos. 2 and 3 were abusing her that she has trapped their rich son.
4. The first informant also states that she was suffering from cancer before marriage and accused No.1 even after knowing the same, married and stayed with her.
But thereafter, he had not stayed with her, even during her pregnancy and that she was being treated as a servant.
5. It is stated that during Nov-2014, she was physically abused by accused No.1 and he tried to strangulate her, which made her to file a police complaint.
There was reconciliation between the couple and they agreed to go for NC: 2024:KHC:32199 divorce by mutual consent by taking some money for herself and her child.
She had looked for an alternative house.

It is alleged that the accused have mentally and physically tortured her due to her history of cancer and therefore,
requested the police to register the case and to initiate legal action.
Accordingly, the police have registered the case.
After investigation, the charge sheet came to be filed for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 506 read with Section 34 of IPC.
However, Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act were dropped for lack of materials.
6. After filing of the charge sheet, the petitioners have filed this petition for quashing the criminal proceedings initiated against them.

7. Heard Sri. Ashok B Patil, learned counsel for petitioner Nos.2 and 3, Smt. K.P.Yashodha, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 and Smt. Anita Abraham, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the materials on records.

sentences.text: 8. Learned counsel for the petitioners contended that petitioner No.1, being accused No.2 is already dead and the NC: 2024:KHC:32199 petition filed by him abated.
Petitioner No.2, being accused No.3 is the mother-in-law and petitioner No.3, being accused No.4 is the brother-in-law of the informant.
He submitted that accused No.1 and the informant were classmates and it was a love marriage.
They have got registered their marriage on 28.11.2006, later, they lived together.
These petitioners are permanent residents of Pune, whereas, accused No.1 and the informant were residing in Bengaluru, pursuing their avocations.
They have begotten a daughter and respondent No.2, who was having passion towards Madhubani Art, resigned from her job to pursue her hobby commercially.

He placed reliance on the publications produced as per Annexures-B and C in support of his contention that the informant had not resigned her job due to pressure from the accused, but only to pursue her passion.
9. Learned counsel further submitted that when the couple could not get on together, it was the informant who sent the draft divorce petition as they have agreed for mutual consent divorce.

However, after going through the final draft and the allegations made therein, accused No.1 send a mail withdrawing his consent for mutual consent divorce as several NC: 2024:KHC:32199 false allegations were made and huge sum of money was said to have been agreed to be paid by accused No.1 towards the alimony for the informant and her child.
Learned counsel for the petitioners referred to the mail dated 30.03.2015 in which, the informant quoted Rs.50Lakhs as alimony.

It is only thereafter, on 01.04.2015 the first information came to be filed against accused Nos.1 to 4.
10.
Learned counsel submitted that bald and general allegations are made against accused Nos. 2 to 4, who are the petitioners herein for having demanded additional dowry and treated her with cruelty.

The police have filed the charge sheet only for the offence punishable under Sections 498A,
506 read with Section 34, by dropping the allegations for the offence punishable under Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act for lack of any materials and the same was not challenged by respondent No.2.
11.
Learned counsel further submitted that respondent No.2 has filed Crl.Misc.No.75/2015 alleging domestic violence against accused No.1.
She got it transferred to Court at Delhi as she is now residing there and the same is still pending.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that all these facts and circumstances disclose that filing the first information against all the family members, who are the permanent residents of Pune was purely an after-thought of and it is a deliberate harassment to extract money.
This development has taken place only after accused No.1 refused to give mutual consent divorce by paying huge sum of alimony.

He placed reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Chandralekha and Others v/s State of Rajasthan and Another1, Rajesh Sharma and Others v/s State of Uttar Pradesh and Another2 and Bhaskar Lal Sharma and Another v/s Monica3 in support of his contention that the Hon'ble Apex Court time and again cautioned the Court not to initiate criminal actions against the family members on the basis of bald and general allegations without there being any basis and it is a classic example of such misuse of the penal provisions, which compel the family members and the husband to agree for any terms.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2 opposing the petition submitted that serious allegations are made against accused Nos.1 to 4.

In the first information, the informant stated that,
she was being harassed for additional dowry.

In fact, respondent No.2 had paid Rs.3,25,000/-
through DD, which was credited to the joint account of accused Nos.2 to 4, that is why she stated she was being treated with cruelty for additional dowry.
She has narrated the act of the petitioners in treating her with cruelty.
Respondent No.2 will have to prove these allegations during trial and it is too premature at this stage to form any opinion and to quash the criminal proceedings.

She has placed reliance on 4 decisions of the co-ordinate bench of this Court in Mohammed Ayaz v/s State of K a r n a t a k a a n d A n r 4 , P r a s h a n t a n d O r s v / s S t a t e o f K a r n a t a k a a n d A n r 5 , S r i PrashanthaMuddukannavara and Ors v/s State of Karnataka and Anr6 and Vijaykumar and Ors v.s State of Karntaka and Anr7 in support of her contention that the co-ordinate benches of this Court categorically held that the allegations made in the first Crl.P.No.101325/2019 DD 01.12.2021 Crl.P.201407/2021 DD 21.12.2021 Crl.P.No.101627/2020 DD 25.11.2021 Crl.P.No.201010/2020 DD 29.11.2021 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:32199 information and the charge sheet are required to be proved during trial and it is too premature at this stage to state that no offence was committed by the petitioners and hence,
prays for dismissal of the petition.
14.

sentences.text: Learned High Court Government Pleader opposing the petition submits that respondent No.2 had made specific allegations.
Based on the same, charge sheet is filed which makes out prima facie case against the petitioners and therefore, the criminal proceedings initiated against them is not liable to be quashed.
Accordingly, prays for dismissal of the petition.

15. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the Petitioners have made out any grounds to allow the petition and to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:32199 REASONS 16.
It is the specific contention of respondent No.2 that she married accused No.1, by registering their marriage on 28.11.2006.

There is no dispute that it was a love marriage as respondent No.2 Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3683453/
5 and accused No.1 were studying together.

entities.text: Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is also not in dispute that respondent No.2 was suffering from cancer and in spite of that accused No.1 married her.
Of course it is stated that she successfully overcome from the aliment and she begotten a child.
It is not in dispute that petitioner Nos.1 to 3 were the permanent residents of Pune, while accused No.1 and respondent No.2 were residing in Bengaluru and pursuing their job in private company.

It is alleged by respondent No.2 that she was demanded to pay additional dowry and she was abused by the petitioners by referring to her poor status of not being able to pay dowry and she was forced to resign to look after her child as these petitioners have not supported her in bringing up the child.

17. Learned counsel for the petitioners placed reliance on the publications produced as per Annexures-B and C, wherein, it is highlighted that respondent No.2 who was having - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:32199 passion towards Madhubani Art, quit her IT job for promoting her passion.
These publications are also not disputed by the learned counsel for respondent No.2 and now it is stated that she has shifted her residence to Delhi where she is pursuing the art of Madhubani.

18. With these background, this court has to consider the allegations made against the petitioners by respondent No.2.
19.

Even though it is contended that the petitioners were demanding for additional dowry from respondent No.2, when it is admitted fact that it is a love marriage and the petitioners are residing in Pune, strong prima facie materials should have been placed to attract Sections 3 and 4 of DP Act.
Admittedly, except the bald allegations regarding demand for additional dowry, no other materials are placed before the Investigating Officer.
Therefore, the Investigating Officer has dropped Sections 3 & 4 of DP Act, while filing the charge sheet.

But Strangely, it is the contention of learned counsel for respondent No.2, while addressing her arguments that a sum of Rs.3,25,000/- was paid by her by way of DD to her father-in- - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:32199 law.
The DD was en-cashed through joint account of accused Nos. 2 to 4 on 22.11.2008.
Unfortunately, there is no such allegations in the first information or in her statement recorded by the Investigating Officer under Section 161 of Cr.PC.
Admittedly, respondent No.2 has not challenged dropping of penal provisions under DP Act while filing the final report.
Therefore, it is to be concluded that the allegations are being made for the sake of maintaining the criminal proceedings against these petitioners.
20. The next contention raised by learned counsel for respondent No.2 is that there was physical and mental cruelty caused to respondent No.2 by these petitioners.
But admittedly, the petitioners are the residents of Pune while, accused No.1 and respondent No.2 were the residents of Bengaluru.
There is reference to few utterances by the petitioners regarding her poor background, abusing her and ill- treating her.

Except the bald and general allegations, I do not find any details as to when Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3683453/
6 such incident had taken place, who abused her and where.

entities.text: Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is also no explanation as to why there was no complaint filed by respondent No.2 against any of these petitioners at the earliest.
The documents that are placed before the Court disclose that after few years of birth of the child,
respondent No.2 quit her job in Information Technology field
. The mail referred to as per Annexures-B and C discloses that she voluntarily quit the job to pursue her passion in Madhubani art.
But now the allegation is that she was forced to quit her job to look after the child as there was no family support.
Even if this allegation is to be accepted, the petitioners cannot be compelled to look after the child of accused Nos.1 and respondent No.2 to pursue their avocation.
That cannot be considered as a cruelty, as the petitioners are not obliged to look after the child, permitting respondent No.2 to pursue her job.
But by going through Annexures - B and C, prima facie the allegations made by respondent No.2 do not get any support.
22. It is pertinent to note that the first information came to be filed on 01.04.2015 and the case under Section 12 of The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005 was filed on 13.04.2015.

entities.text: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
So simultaneously respondent No.2 chosen to initiate action against accused No.1 by filing the criminal complaint and also by filing Crl.Misc.No.75/2015,
- 15 - NC: 2024:KHC:32199 which is said to be still pending in Court at Delhi, where respondent No.2 is staying.
23. It is the contention of learned counsel for respondent No.2 that she was treated with cruelty by demanding additional dowry during 2008 i.e., after two years of registering their marriage.
Even though respondent No.2 had filed the first information regarding cruelty, it is only against accused No.1 by alleging that he tried to strangulate her.
In that complaint there is no allegation of any ill-treatment or any cruelty caused to her by these petitioners.

It is also pertinent to note that admittedly, there was exchange of legal notices between the parties during Feb-2015 and even in that legal notice, there is no allegation against any of these petitioners for having committed any of the criminal offence.
It is suffice to say, while filing first information on 01.04.2015, bald and general allegations are made against accused No.2 and 4 who are the in-laws.
I do not find any sufficient ground to keep criminal proceedings pending against them.

24. Learned counsel for the petitioners placed reliance on the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in Chandralekha and - 16 - Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3683453/
7 NC: 2024:KHC:32199 Others (supra), wherein the Court after taking into consideration the nature and allegations thought it as a fit case for quashing the criminal proceedings as no specific role is attributed to any of the accused and no steps were taken to file any complaint within a reasonable time, but later, a police complaint came to be filed trying to rope in all the family members of the husband.
25.

entities.text:
Chandralekha and - 16 - Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3683453/
7 NC: 2024:KHC:32199 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Rajesh Sharma and others (supra) the Hon'ble Apex Court referred to the objective with which Section 498A of IPC inserted in the statute i.e., with the laudable object of punishing cruelty at the hands of husband or his relatives against a wife and highlighted filing of such complaints under Section 498A of IPC alleging harassment of a married women with bald and general allegations for trivial issues, which was held to be not maintainable.
The Court has also referred to the directions issued in Arnesh Kumar vs State Of Bihar & Anr 8 to avoid much damage that was being caused to the fabric of family.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar vs State Of Bihar & Anr 8
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court also issued several directions for establishing the Family Welfare Committees at the district level.
However, said direction was later set aside.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Bhaskar Lal Sharma (supra) highlighted the requirement of Section 498A of IPC in paragraph No.30 as under:
"30.

For proving the offence under Section 498-A IPC, the complainant must make allegation of harassment to the extent so as to coerce her to meet any unlawful demand of dowry, or any wilful conduct on the part of the accused of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide or to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health.

We do not find any such allegation has been made or otherwise can be found out so as to enable us to arrive at an opinion that the appellants prima facie have committed such an offence. "
27.

The Court has also referred to its earlier decision in Noorjahan v/s State9 by extracting paragraph No.17, which reads as under:
"17.

The object for which Section 498-A IPC was introduced is amply reflected in the Statement of Objects and Reasons while enacting the Criminal Law (Amendment)
Act, 1983 (46 of 1983).
As clearly stated therein the increase in the number of dowry deaths is a matter of serious concern.

The extent of the evil has been commented upon by the Joint Committee of the Houses to examine the work of the Dowry Prohibition (2008) 11 SCC 55 - 18 - Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3683453/
8 NC: 2024:KHC:32199 Act, 1961.

entities.text: Dowry Prohibition (2008) 11 SCC 55 - 18 - Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In some cases, cruelty of the husband and the relatives of the husband which culminate in suicide by or murder of the helpless woman concerned, constitute only a small fraction involving such cruelty.

Therefore, it was proposed to amend IPC, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and the Evidence Act suitably to deal effectively not only with cases of dowry deaths but also cases of cruelty to married a women by the husband, in-laws and relatives.

The avowed object is to combat the menace of dowry death and cruelty."
28.

The Court has also referred to its decision in Sushil Kumar v/s Union Bank of India10 by extracting paragraph Nos. 10, which reads as under:
" 10.

entities.text: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

All police officers be provided with a check list containing specified sub-clauses under Section 41(1)(b)(ii);
(2005) 6 SCC 281 - 19 - NC: 2024:KHC:32199 11.3. The police officer shall forward the check list duly filled and furnish the reasons and materials which necessitated the arrest, while forwarding/producing the accused before the Magistrate for further detention; 11.4.

The Magistrate while authorising detention of the accused shall peruse the report furnished by the police officer in terms aforesaid and only after recording its satisfaction, the Magistrate will authorise detention; 11.5.

The decision not to arrest an accused, be forwarded to the Magistrate within two weeks from the date of the institution of the case with a copy to the Magistrate which may be extended by the Superintendent of Police of the district for the reasons to be recorded in writing;
11.6. Notice of appearance in terms of Section 41-A CrPC be served on the accused within two weeks from the date of institution of the case, which may be extended by the Superintendent of Police of the district for the reasons to be recorded in writing; 11.7.

Failure to comply with the directions aforesaid shall apart from rendering the police officers concerned liable for departmental action,
they shall also be liable to be punished for contempt of court to be instituted before the High Court having territorial jurisdiction.
11.8. Authorising detention without recording reasons as aforesaid by the Judicial Magistrate concerned shall be liable for departmental action by the appropriate High Court."

- 20 - NC: 2024:KHC:32199 Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3683453/
9 29.

Finally, the Court has referred to its decision in State of Haryana v/s Bhajan Lal11 to reiterate the ground on which, the criminal proceedings could be quashed and extracted in paragraph No.40 as under:
" 40.

entities.text: State of Haryana v/s Bhajan Lal11
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The jurisdiction of the High Court to quash an order of summoning and/or a criminal proceeding as also this Court are well known.
The parties have relied upon the decisions of this Court in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal4.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal4
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
We may notice Categories 1, 3, 5 and 7 mentioned in para 102 of the said decision, which are as under: (SCC pp. 378-79) "(1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.
(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.
(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
1992 Supp(1) SCC 335 - 21 - NC: 2024:KHC:32199 (7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with malafide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."
30.

If these decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court are applied to the facts and circumstances of the present case, I am fully convinced that it is nothing but a bald and general allegations made by respondent No.2 to rope in the father-in- law, mother-in-law and brother-in-law, to see that they face the criminal trial, which is nothing but an abuse of process of law.

31. The decisions relied on by the learned counsel for respondent No.2, which are rendered by this Court and the co- ordinate benches are on facts and circumstances of the individual cases and the same cannot be applied to the present case as the facts are entirely different.

32. Under these circumstance, I am of the opinion that there are no reasons to permit the criminal proceedings to continue against the petitioners as it would amount to infringement of the right of the petitioners and also abuse of - 22 - Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/3683453/
10 NC: 2024:KHC:32199 the process of the Court.

entities.text: Parasmal vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, I am of the opinion that the criminal proceeding is liable to be quashed.

33. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the Affirmative and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is allowed.
(ii) Criminal proceedings initiated against the accused Nos. 2 to 4 in C.C.No.20004/2015, on the file of learned V Additional CMM, Bangalore, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 506 read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, is hereby quashed.
Registry to communicate the order to the Jurisdictional Magistrate forthwith.

" 40.
The parties have relied upon the decisions of this Court in State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal4.
We may notice Categories 1, 3, 5 and 7 mentioned in para 102 of the said decision, which are as under: (SCC pp. 378-79) "(1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.
(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.
(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.
1992 Supp(1) SCC 335 - 21 - NC: 2024:KHC:32199 (7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with malafide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."
